text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to evaluate this newborn who is presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting. Can you tell me the infant's age in days and whether they have passed any meconium stool since birth?

text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. text: The physical findings of epicanthal folds, upward slanting eyes, low-set ears, and a single transverse palmar crease are classic features of Down syndrome. Newborns with Down syndrome have a significantly increased risk of duodenal atresia, which presents with bilious vomiting and feeding intolerance. DIAGNOSIS READY: Duodenal Atresia
